newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-Reuters says cash return at limit.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Reuters says cash return at limit.

text.p: Global news and information group Reuters Holdings is returning as much cash to shareholders as it can efficiently under existing British tax rules, chief executive Peter Job said on Wednesday.
Earlier, Reuters said it intended to repurchase up to 200 million stg of its shares over the next 12 months.
"If you go beyond a certain limit you simply get involved in unrecoverable tax which is not very good for shareholders," Job said in an interview.
"We're making this as big as we can within the tax capacity we have. Up to 200 million (stg) is about where we can go."
Reuters said the plan would offset the expected growth in net funds, which stood at 1.12 billion pounds as of June 30.
"The effect of this will be to stop the accumulation of cash in the enterprise but not to come to grips with the excess cash we're holding, which we would rather shareholders had."
"We don't want to be pushed into lax management through the availability of cash mountains or into inappropriate acquisitions," he added.
Job said Reuters did not rule out large acquisitions but said it was hard to find companies that offered genuine synergies.
He said the company would phase out obsolete products as it headed into the millennium, streamlining its range and reducing what he termed "product clutter".

He said the 3000 series continued to sell well and was on target to meet its target of 30,000 sales by the end of the year. Orders for 3000 products now total 24,300, of which 10,600 have been installed. New users account for 17 percent of these sales.
